newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentine envoy blasts Brazil cenbank official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine envoy blasts Brazil cenbank official.

text.p: The Argentine ambassador to Brazil blasted a senior central bank official for "treason" in the way Brasilia changed its import financing rules without warning its Mercosur trade bloc partners, newspapers reported.

Invited to a what appeared to have been a hot-blooded lunch Thursday with Argentine envoy Diego Guelar, newspapers said he had stressed that taking Mercosur by surprise with the import financing move had created a "negative climate".
"I think you can call it treason," Gazeta Mercantil quoted him as saying in a reference to the way Central Bank Director of International Affairs Gustavo Franco announced the measures.
Guelar said the most serious problem was that Brazil had "taken its partners by surprise, creating a negative climate."
The Argentine embassy declined comment and said the ambassador was travelling.

"If (Finance Minister Pedro) Malan had heard how the the ambassador referred to the Director of International Affairs at the Central Bank, Gustavo Franco, he would decide not to include him in a Central Bank delegation which will accompany him to Asuncion on April 23," Globo columnist Tereza Cruvinel wrote.
Brazil at the end of last month restricted short-term import financing of less than 360 days, effectively forcing importers to pay in cash.
Under pressure from Mercosur partners Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay and the group's free trade associates Chile and Bolivia, Brazil agreed to give the bloc a partial exemption for 120 days.

Finance Minister Malan conceded as he made the allowance that Brazil should have informed its partners in advance and said a special subgroup for macroeconomic coordination would be set up within Mercosur to ensure it did in the future.
Argentina is not the only country still disgruntled about the new rules. Paraguay Thursday called an emergency Mercosur summit for April 23 in Asuncion to discuss the issue.
